A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same literature-review evaluation framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved into v3 Appendices C and D.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of four LLMs, including reference accuracy, abstract quality, disciplinary comparisons, and overlap with human citations in Tables 1–4 and Section 4.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of five LLMs, adds review-content results, and reports human validation of reference assessment in Section 4.6.

M1.justification: v3 extends the proposed evaluator with GPT-4 extraction of review key points followed by NLI-based Key Point Recall scoring. This adds a scoring component; the three generation tasks, Appendix A prompts, and reference-matching procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use 2023 Annual Reviews articles from the same 51 journals and discipline groups for reference generation, abstract writing, and review composition. The added content metrics and human validation assess retained tasks and outputs. The reported article-count revision does not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: DeepSeek-V3 joins the evaluated comparison set in Tables 1–4 and corresponding analyses. Qwen-2.5-72B, Llama-3.2-3B, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.5-Sonnet are retained, making this a limited expansion of the model comparison.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces journal-level aggregation with article-level averaging for reference accuracy, title search rate, and entailment. v3 also introduces Task 3 evaluation using ten extracted key points and ROUGE, plus validation on 100 references judged by three annotators using majority vote. The reported dataset total changes from 1,106 to 1,105, although disciplinary counts remain unchanged and sum to 1,106. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds human validation of the reference detector in Section 4.6, analysis of correctly cited references by publication year in Figure 2, and disciplinary analysis of review key-point coverage in Figure 4(d). These substantially expand the questions examined. Existing metadata and citation-overlap analyses remain, with the latter's detailed discussion moved to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions use one-way ANOVA, but v3 reports p-values without the F statistics supplied in v1. v3 also introduces kappa agreement between automatic reference judgments and majority-vote human judgments. Neither version reports repeated-generation run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v3 adds DeepSeek-V3 results and Task 3 content scores: Claude leads KPR at 62.32, while DeepSeek leads the reported ROUGE metrics. Existing values also change alongside revised aggregation; for example, Claude's TRUE score in Table 2 changes from 78.10 to 78.90. Llama's Task 1 disciplinary ANOVA changes from p<.001 to p=0.065. New human-validation results report 86% accuracy and kappa 0.71. These are revised or added results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of aggregate accuracy, title search rate, and entailment change from journal-based aggregation to article averages, beyond merely renumbering equations. v3 Equation 8 additionally defines review key-point recall over extracted claim sets. Neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes the introduction's assertion that no comprehensive prior evaluation of LLM literature-review writing exists. The automatic three-task framework and central findings about hallucinations and disciplinary variation remain. The former conclusion, retained in Appendix D, extends its broad Claude-superiority claim to include DeepSeek-V3.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new human agreement results as supporting the reference detector's reliability and motivates key-point evaluation through the difficulty of directly comparing lengthy reviews. Existing explanations involving training data and author names in generated prose largely remain through relocation. The limitations paragraph is substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies implementation choices for the new content evaluation: GPT-4 extracts ten key points, GPT-4o supplies NLI judgments, and concatenated key points serve as ROUGE comparison text. Appendix A's generation prompts are unchanged. The future Hugging Face deployment statement moves to Appendix D without announcing newly available code or data.

R1.justification: v3 adds Agarwal et al. on literature-review generation, Wang et al. (2024a) on academic literature use, and Qi et al. on Key Point Recall. It removes the OpenAI, Bubeck, and Ji references accompanying the general hallucination taxonomy. This selectively refocuses positioning toward literature-review evaluation while retaining AutoSurvey and the main citation-hallucination studies.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related-work prose are extensively rewritten, with additional clarification throughout the methodology and results. Most of the original conclusion becomes Appendix D, and detailed citation-overlap discussion becomes Appendix C. These changes substantially revise both language and narrative organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, a citation-year plot is added, and the three disciplinary charts are consolidated with a new KPR panel into v3 Figure 4. Table 3 expands into separate reference and review-content groups, and comparison plots accommodate DeepSeek-V3. The overlap radar moves to Appendix C, while the unchanged dataset-distribution graphic is resized and placed below the prompt table.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful evidence missing from v1: review-content measurements beyond citation accuracy in Table 3 and human validation of the reference detector, reporting 86% accuracy and kappa 0.71. These strengthen the evaluation, but the validation sample lacks selection details and reporting inconsistencies remain or arise: the revised dataset total conflicts with disciplinary counts, and Claude's TRUE score remains 78.10 in prose despite becoming 78.90 in Table 2. The net quality gain is positive but qualified.
